newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Sudan says peace process will go on without Garang.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says peace process will go on without Garang.

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir said on Monday his government would proceed with a peace agreement it signed with some of its minor rivals even if main rebel leader John Garang refuses to join it.
"We would like Garang to join but if he refuses the peace process will continue without him," Bashir told a news conference at an Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit in Harare.

The Khartoum government signed a peace agreement with several opposition groups on April 21 which it says is comprehensive enough to address "all the problems of Sudan", including the basis of the Garang rebellion.

Garang's rebel army has fought since 1983 for greater autonomy of the Christian and animist south from the Moslem, Arabised north and has launched a series of offensives this year, the most successful since 1991.
A spokesman for Garang's Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) dismissed Bashir's press conference as diplomatic propaganda aimed at painting Garang as a rebel without a cause.
"Serious negotiations and agreements are not part discussed this way, only propaganda," the SPLA's Samson Kwaje told reporters.
